The Family Medicaid Planning Checklist

What to organize now, what to ask a professional about and what to keep an eye on.

Download PDF

Mom is managing on her own, and nothing needs deciding today. That leaves room for a list. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is simply something for another day, not a sign that anything is wrong.

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you organize, ask and keep watch. It doesn't say what any item means for Mom, what should be done now or what can wait, or whether anything on it is a concern. Rules vary by state, and nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice. Those questions go to your Medicaid planner or the appropriate licensed professional, and to the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You've sorted what to organize, what to ask about and what to keep an eye on. The planning interview picks up from there: it asks about your family's situation and gives you a free planning report you can bring to any conversation about paying for care.

Where this comes from

The item marked 1 follows AARP's legal checklist for family caregivers, which suggests making sure family members know where the documents are. The rest come from the Medicaid Planning Roadmap's own working list for this step.
